why: I compared each verifier PASS/FAIL condition with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 3 and 5 test only what their words require. Check 2 fails an "altered" path, which matches "exactly as passed". Check 5 says to read the failing test to confirm it asserts the file path, which the words require. The advisory items are correctly kept under "Advisory". Check 4 goes further than its words. The expect line says the app "prints `listening on 9000` on stdout", but the PASS condition says "stdout is `listening on 9000`" and the FAIL condition is "anything else". That demands exact stdout equality. An app that printed `listening on 9000` plus another line would meet the expect line's words but fail this check. So an exact-output test the words do not force sits inside a PASS/FAIL condition instead of under Advisory.
